questions.question: At whose house does Savita and Pran's wedding take place, and in which locality of Brahmpur does that house stand?
questions.answer: It takes place at Prem Nivas, the Kapoor family house, in the locality of Pasand Bagh.

questions.question: Why did Mahesh Kapoor, the groom's father, end up hosting the wedding instead of the bride's family?
questions.answer: Mrs Rupa Mehra's father, who was supposed to host, took sudden umbrage a fortnight before the wedding, locked up his house and disappeared, so the Minister stepped in.

questions.question: How many times did the bride and groom walk around the sacred fire?
questions.answer: Seven times.

questions.question: Mahesh Kapoor wanted a particular kind of performer at the wedding. Who was it, and why did Mrs Rupa Mehra refuse?
questions.answer: He wanted a renowned ghazal singer (a courtesan); Mrs Rupa Mehra refused because 'that sort of person' meant a Muslim and a courtesan.

questions.question: What was Dr Kishen Chand Seth's profession, and what was his diet restricted to?
questions.answer: He was a radiologist (septuagenarian); his diet was boiled eggs, weak tea, lemon squash and arrowroot biscuits.

questions.question: Where does Arun Mehra work, what is his brother Varun studying, and where do the two of them live?
questions.answer: Arun is an executive at Bentsen & Pryce in Calcutta; Varun studies mathematics at Calcutta University and lives with Arun and Meenakshi in Calcutta.

questions.question: Whom is Arun married to, which family does she come from, and what bothered Mrs Rupa Mehra about the match?
questions.answer: He is married to Meenakshi, a Chatterji (daughter of Mr Justice Chatterji of the Calcutta High Court); Mrs Rupa Mehra disliked that he married outside the khatri caste.

questions.question: What does Arun look down on about the Kapoors and the wedding celebrations?
questions.answer: He finds them provincial and crass: the rustic relatives and state politicians, the coloured lights in the hedge, the pomegranate juice instead of alcohol, and Maan running a cloth shop in Banaras.

questions.question: How old are Bhaskar and Aparna at the time of the outing to the zoo?
questions.answer: Bhaskar is nine and Aparna is a third of his age, i.e. three.

questions.question: What is Malati Trivedi studying and at which college, and under whom does she learn classical singing?
questions.answer: She is a medical student at the Prince of Wales Medical College and studies classical singing under Ustad Majeed Khan.

questions.question: Why did old Mrs Tandon flinch when the Nawab Sahib mentioned Pakistan?
questions.answer: Her family had fled the riots in Lahore three years earlier, lost most of their wealth, and her son Kedarnath was scarred in an attack on their convoy.

questions.question: How did Kedarnath get the scars on his hands, and what trade did he take up after returning to Brahmpur?
questions.answer: Rioters attacked his convoy of army trucks near the Ravi Bridge during Partition and he caught a spear blade with his hands; in Brahmpur he went into the shoe trade.

questions.question: Who saved the convoy Kedarnath was travelling in when it was attacked near the Ravi Bridge?
questions.answer: A Gurkha regiment coming from the other side opened fire and the attackers fled.

questions.question: What plant is Lata named after, and how did Lata react when her mother told her she must cling to her husband?
questions.answer: She is named after a vine; her mother said she must cling to her husband and Lata repeated 'Cling?' with quiet scorn.

questions.question: Where did the group go in the tonga the morning after the wedding, and what did Varun say was special about the Brahmpur race-course?
questions.answer: They went to the zoo; Varun said it is the only anti-clockwise race-course in India other than Lucknow.

questions.question: How does Dr Kishen Chand Seth insist his nimbu pani be made, and why?
questions.answer: With salt (and pepper) rather than sugar, because he is diabetic and sugar is poison for him.

questions.question: How old is the servant Mansoor and whom is he standing in for?
questions.answer: He is sixteen and is standing in for his father, who had taken a short leave.

questions.question: Why did Mrs Rupa Mehra decide not to put golden numerals showing the age on Parvati's birthday card?
questions.answer: Parvati was only 35, ten years younger than Rupa; the '35' would imply an unacceptable age disparity (and an unacceptable motive for marrying her father).

questions.question: What match did Dr Seth suggest for Lata, and what did he say about a possible double wedding involving Maan?
questions.answer: He suggested a young radiologist at the Prince of Wales; he said they could have captured Maan for a double wedding, but Maan was now said to be engaged to a Banaras girl.

questions.question: What happened when Mrs Rupa Mehra and her four children went to live with her father after her husband's death?
questions.answer: It lasted only a few months and was a disaster; Seth accused her of making eyes at his colleagues, Arun threatened to beat him up, and she left with the children for Darjeeling.

questions.question: Whom did Mrs Rupa Mehra write to for help in finding a match for Lata, and during which holiday did she propose they visit?
questions.answer: She wrote to Kalpana (Mr Gaur's daughter) in Delhi and proposed visiting during Divali (or the Christmas-New Year holidays).

questions.question: What was Raghubir Mehra's gift to his wife when their son Arun was born?
questions.answer: A black and gold Mont Blanc fountain pen.

questions.question: Who runs the Imperial Book Depot and on which street is it located?
questions.answer: The brothers Yashwant and Balwant run it, on Nabiganj.

questions.question: What does the young man who talks to Lata in the bookshop say he studies, and what does his father teach?
questions.answer: He is a history student; his father teaches maths at the university.

questions.question: Haresh takes Bhaskar to meet a certain Dr Durrani. Who is Dr Durrani's son, and why does Haresh want Bhaskar to meet him?
questions.answer: Dr Durrani's son is Kabir; Haresh thinks Bhaskar's interest in mathematics is remarkable and wants him to meet the mathematician.

questions.question: What did Bhaskar take away with him from Dr Durrani's house?
questions.answer: Loops of twisted newspaper, a purple kite and exactly sixteen toothpicks.

questions.question: How much did Haresh pay Jagat Ram for the brogues compared with what he had promised?
questions.answer: One-and-a-half times as much as he had promised.

questions.question: Which writer did Pran want added to the Modern British Literature syllabus, and who led the opposition to it?
questions.answer: James Joyce; Professor O.P. Mishra, the head of the English Department, opposed it.

questions.question: What arguments does Professor Mishra use against putting Joyce on the syllabus?
questions.answer: He says India should not follow the American dissertation mill, that Ulysses and Finnegans Wake are unreadable and unhealthy for students, and that they encourage sloppy writing.

questions.question: Which committee member unexpectedly supported Pran, and which Joyce story did he cite?
questions.answer: Dr Narayanan, a Romantic Revivalist, cited 'The Dead'.

questions.question: How many writers are on the Modern British Literature list, and what position has Pran applied for?
questions.answer: Twenty-one writers; Pran applied for a readership in the department.

questions.question: How did the unrest at Misri Mandi begin?
questions.answer: A fight in a cheap drinking place (the kalari's joint) between a trader's assistant and three jatavs left a man blind in one eye; a crowd of jatavs then gathered at the Govind Shoe Mart and threatened to burn the stall.

questions.question: What orders did Home Minister L.N. Agarwal give District Magistrate Krishan Dayal about Misri Mandi, and what practical objection did the DM raise?
questions.answer: He told him to guard the entrances of the Govind Shoe Mart and disperse pickets, reading Section 144 and firing if necessary; the DM objected that police were tied up at the Shiva Temple site.

questions.question: What combination of events led to the riot in Chowk on the Friday evening?
questions.answer: The Imam's inflammatory sermon about the Shiva Temple, a conch being blown during the call to prayer, and only about fifteen policemen being left at the Chowk police station because the Home Minister had stationed police in Misri Mandi.

questions.question: Whom does the Imam call the guiding spirit of the temple committee?
questions.answer: The 'debauched buffalo of Marh', i.e. the Raja of Marh.

questions.question: How was the police action at Baitar House stopped, and who carried the appeal to the Chief Minister?
questions.answer: Zainab wrote a letter that Murtaza Ali and little Hassan carried to the Chief Minister, who phoned Agarwal and ordered him to call it off and make the police leave.

questions.question: On what legal pretext did L.N. Agarwal plan to act against Baitar House?
questions.answer: He thought part of Baitar House could be treated as evacuee property because Begum Abida Khan's husband had gone to Pakistan, and he phoned the Custodian of Evacuee Property.

questions.question: How did the Democratic, Socialist and smaller parties vote on the Zamindari Abolition Bill, and what did the Democratic Party do afterwards?
questions.answer: The Democratic Party voted against unanimously, the Socialists reluctantly voted for it ('half a loaf'), smaller parties and Independents mostly for it; the Democratic Party then walked out.

questions.question: According to Begum Abida Khan, how did the government restructure the compensation to avoid a court challenge?
questions.answer: It split compensation into a non-graduated compensation and a graduated Rehabilitation Grant, moving three-quarters of the money into the grant.

questions.question: On what payment terms were zamindars to be compensated, according to Begum Abida Khan?
questions.answer: Half in government bonds, and the rest in instalments over twenty-five years.

questions.question: How many people did Begum Abida Khan say were being dispossessed by the bill?
questions.answer: Eight lakh people.

questions.question: What does the Nawab Sahib remember about the signatories of the Zamindars' Association petition to the Governor twelve years earlier?
questions.answer: A good third of the signatories had used thumbprints (were illiterate).

questions.question: What two examples of princely extravagance does the Nawab Sahib recall?
questions.answer: A ruler obsessed with dogs, and an opium addict who wanted women thrown into his lap.

questions.question: In Ustad Majeed Khan's class, which raag was Malati learning and which composition was Veena Tandon singing?
questions.answer: Malati was learning Raag Ramkali; Veena sang the composition 'Jaago Mohan Pyaare' (in Raag Bhairava).

questions.question: Which students and which accompanist were in Ustad Majeed Khan's class that morning?
questions.answer: Malati Trivedi, a young man (the boy), two young women, a shy Bengali woman and Veena Tandon, with Motu Chand on tabla.

questions.question: Why was Ustad Majeed Khan upset about the Shiva Temple, and what did he ask Veena to tell her father?
questions.answer: The temple being built in Chowk near his house would let the conch compete with the muezzin's call to prayer; he asked her to tell her father, the Minister, to help protect their religion.

questions.question: What does Ustad Majeed Khan's own family background reveal, and why does it embitter him?
questions.answer: He comes from a family of hereditary sarangi players; he tries to dissociate from the sarangi tradition's link with courtesans, but no kalawant family would marry into his.

questions.question: Why is Ishaq Khan trying to get his brother-in-law moved, and how do artists' grades matter?
questions.answer: He wants his sister's husband, a sarangi player and staff artist, moved from AIR Lucknow to AIR Brahmpur; the Station Director would not swap a B-plus artist like Rafiq for a B-grade one.

questions.question: What gift does Ishaq bring Tasneem and how does Saeeda Bai react to it?
questions.answer: A baby hill parakeet; Saeeda Bai says no more birds in the house ('One singer is enough') and tells him to get rid of it.

questions.question: Why does Firoz come to Saeeda Bai's house, and what does he see there?
questions.answer: He brings the monthly envelope from his father the Nawab Sahib, and meets Tasneem carrying a birdcage.

questions.question: What was served at the four-course dinner when the Coxes dined with Arun and Meenakshi?
questions.answer: Soup, smoked hilsa, roast chicken and a lemon souffle.

questions.question: What does Meenakshi claim is the secret of her family's smoked hilsa, and how had she actually learned it?
questions.answer: She says the secret is the fire, with puffed rice and jaggery thrown on it, but she had only learned this that afternoon from the Mugh cook.

questions.question: What is Shamshu, and where do Varun and his friends buy it and at what price?
questions.answer: A cheap Chinese spirit, bought from a hole-in-the-wall place in Chinatown at eight annas a glass.

questions.question: Who are Mr Justice Chatterji's five children, and what occupies each of them?
questions.answer: Amit writes poetry, Meenakshi plays canasta, Dipankar seeks the Meaning of Life, Kakoli keeps the telephone busy, and Tapan (twelve or thirteen) goes to the boarding school Jheel.

questions.question: What is Amit Chatterji's new novel about?
questions.answer: A moneylender at the time of the Bengal Famine.

questions.question: What breed was the dog Cuddles sold as, what is he really, and who was his most recent victim?
questions.answer: Sold as an Apso, he is a mutt with a large proportion of Tibetan terrier; his latest victim was the census-taker.

questions.question: Who is Biswas Babu, and what did he advise Meenakshi about her marriage?
questions.answer: He is the Chatterji family's old clerk (originally Mr Justice Chatterji's father's clerk) and he advised Meenakshi against marrying Arun.

questions.question: What book did Dr Ila Chattopadhyay write, and what did she think of the ghazal singer's performance she attended in Brahmpur?
questions.answer: She wrote 'Metaphysical Causality', a book about Donne; she found the ghazal singer (Saeeda something) dreadful and the self-pitying verse insipid.

questions.question: Why did the Chatterjis have reservations about Meenakshi's marriage to Arun?
questions.answer: He was not a Brahmo, Brahmin or Bengali, i.e. outside the community, and his family was struggling financially.

questions.question: What worries the Chatterjis about Kakoli's latest admirer, and what is his job?
questions.answer: He is a foreigner, a Second Secretary at the German Consulate General, who keeps inviting her to diplomatic functions.

questions.question: From whom did Arun inherit his atrocious temper, and what shows that he alone could defy that person?
questions.answer: From his grandfather Dr Kishen Chand Seth; Arun once threatened to beat him up and took his Buick on a catastrophic joyride, yet was loved the more for it.

questions.question: What marriage was being arranged for Maan, with whom, and where did Dr Seth say the engagement stood?
questions.answer: Mahesh Kapoor had written to the Banaras people about a bride; Dr Seth heard that Maan was already engaged to the Banaras girl.

questions.question: Why does L.N. Agarwal gloat over Mahesh Kapoor's son?
questions.answer: Because of the gossip that Maan is involved with the courtesan Saeeda Bai ('lies at the feet of prostitutes').

questions.question: Whose breathlessness is said to resemble Pran's asthma, and what triggers it in April?
questions.answer: Mrs Mahesh Kapoor's; her allergy to neem blossoms.

questions.question: How does Ustad Majeed Khan's own background make his contempt for Ishaq Khan's instrument ironic?
questions.answer: Majeed Khan comes from a hereditary family of sarangi players and is trying to dissociate himself from that tradition, yet he calls sarangi players a distraction.

questions.question: What is the name of Mrs Rupa Mehra's pet dog?
questions.answer: The text gives Mrs Rupa Mehra no dog; Cuddles is the Chatterji family's dog (Dipankar's).

questions.question: Why did Savita's father, Raghubir Mehra, give her away at her wedding?
questions.answer: He was dead (eight years); Savita was given away by her mother, Mrs Rupa Mehra.

questions.question: Why did Dr Kishen Chand Seth give a speech at his granddaughter Savita's wedding?
questions.answer: He did not attend; he had gone off to Delhi for a conference of cardiologists.

questions.question: How much dowry did the Mehras pay to the Kapoors for Savita's marriage?
questions.answer: None: Mahesh Kapoor never asked for any dowry and would not let Mrs Rupa Mehra pay for the wedding.

questions.question: Where did Pran and Savita spend their honeymoon in Darjeeling?
questions.answer: They went to Simla for a week's honeymoon, not Darjeeling.

questions.question: Why did Lata attend Pran's class on the Romantic poets?
questions.answer: Lata attended his class on the Elizabethans, not the Romantic poets.

questions.question: Why did Lata decide to become a medical doctor like Malati?
questions.answer: She did not; Lata studies English at Brahmpur University (and once wanted to become a nun), while Malati is the medical student.

questions.question: How did Pran overcome Professor Mishra's objection that Joyce could not be taught because of the rule about living writers?
questions.answer: The tradition excludes writers alive during the Second World War; Joyce died in 1941, but Pran pointed out that T.S. Eliot, who is alive, had been granted a waiver and proposed a waiver for Joyce too; Dr Narayanan and Dr Gupta agreed.

questions.question: What is the full text of the poem Amit Chatterji wrote about the young bride?
questions.answer: The poem's text is never quoted; it is only mentioned in passing.

questions.question: Whom does Lata finally choose to marry at the end of the novel?
questions.answer: The provided portion of the book does not reach the end; her choice is not stated in the document.
